title: After the Water Clears

beats.t: Just before the second syllable appeared, something black covered Yeoni's view. Not a cold palm. Umbrella fabric.
Seo Hanbi held the taped umbrella open before the nameplate. The umbrella that had been tucked beside Yeoni's bag. One crooked rib blocked the name perfectly.
Don't read. Three steps back. Now.
Hide a name with one umbrella? You always act that way, rainwater.
Yes. Always. And this time, I'll keep doing it to the end.
Yeoni, close your eyes and move back. Moka, some fire.
Moka struck a match. A small flame drew a circle at their feet. The ivy reaching from the door hesitated before it. They backed into the room of Card Five.
This fire won't last! I've got three matches left!
The door closed behind them. Ivy covered the nameplate again. Black Moon's voice was sealed inside.
Card Five's room resembled an old cathedral. Starlight entered through high windows. They gathered beneath a pillar. Moka's little fire burned on the floor.
Door Six won't open at night. That's when names are most blurred. We hold out here until morning.
Then I'm sleeping first. Yundal, you're on watch. No asking birthdays.
Watch duty is boring. Nobody to ask.
Instead of answering, Moka began snoring. Whether he was asleep or simply refusing to listen was unclear. Yundal smiled and walked around the pillar, deliberately leaving the two alone.
Neo lay against Yeoni's shoulder, breathing unevenly. Whenever cool light brushed his back, Yeoni paused their hand and searched for warmth again.
(He can't be this light. Am I missing something?)
Across the fire, Seo Hanbi was folding the umbrella. One rib kept sticking out. She folded it, opened it, then folded it again.
That crooked rib's always like that. I repaired it.
I know. Three layers of tape. Two would have been enough.
Three makes me feel better.
Arithmetic worthy of you, Yeoni.
Seo Hanbi offered the umbrella handle-first, so Yeoni could take hold of it immediately.
Let me return this. What you gave me at the bus stop. I left it on the hallway floor.
I picked it up after you threw it away. Finders keepers.
Then it's all the more yours.
No. Since finders keepers makes me the owner, I can give it away if I want.
Yeoni didn't take the umbrella. Instead, they folded Seo Hanbi's hand over its handle and patted it twice, like stamping a contract.
Keep it. It's not a loan. Don't repay me.
Seo Hanbi's other hand drifted unconsciously inside her coat, where the ledger lay. It had shrunk to palm size. Every night, one line was coming undone.
Habit. When I receive something, I try to record it. My hand moves first.
Try. Let's see what happens.
Seo Hanbi picked up her pen and wrote: One umbrella. Before the ink could soak into the paper, a raindrop fell on it. The words became clear water and ran off.
It won't write.
See? Even the ledger says not to repay it.
Seo Hanbi stared at the wet ledger for a long time. Then she gave a very small laugh, soundless, just one shake of her shoulders.
The fire burned lower. Yeoni added a dry scrap of card instead of wood. For an instant, the sparks burst into star shapes.
Hey. Can I ask something?
Anything except the ledger.
What did the me from the first spring call you?
Seo Hanbi's hand stopped. Her fingers tightened around the umbrella handle. The answer didn't come at once.
I think I heard it through the thread. Faintly. But I can't remember the word.
I won't tell you that.
Why? I said it to you. Someone like me, anyway.
Because it was something she gave me. If you say it again, it feels as though she'll truly disappear.
Yeoni fell silent. The fire crackled softly. Neo's eyelids stirred at the sound.
I'm jealous of her. She knew you before I did.
She is you. The same hand tilted that umbrella.
Same hand, different spring. That spring is yours. I shouldn't take it.
Then I'll make a new one. My own.
A new what?
Name to call you. Seo Hanbi is too long. Ms. Seo Hanbi is too distant. And Ms. Tiger is wrong now.
Yeoni traced letters in the air. One, two. Erased them. Wrote again.
Hanbi. Hey, Hanbi.
Seo Hanbi lifted her head, eyes widening. She tried to speak, but only her lips moved. Wet lashes glittered in the firelight.
That's just dropping the surname. Too easy.
Easy is good. So I can call you quickly when it rains.
Only when it rains?
On clear days too. You carry an umbrella on clear days.
Instead of answering, Seo Hanbi hugged the umbrella. Its taped handle touched her chin. She stayed that way for a long time. Then, very softly, she repeated it.
Hanbi. Yes. I'll be Hanbi.
A little rain fell beyond the high windows. It wasn't cold. Dust settled on the cathedral floor, and the air cleared.
For a while, neither spoke. Both held their hands toward the fire. The backs of Yeoni's hands looked a little warmer. Seo Hanbi's were still cold.
Then one more thing. Answer this. What's wrong with Neo?
Wrong?
He makes no footsteps, and his hand passes through cards. He's human again, but his body keeps disappearing. You know why, don't you?
Seo Hanbi looked at Neo. His eyes were closed, but the hand holding Yeoni's sleeve moved a little. He was listening.
That's not my debt, so I can't speak of it.
You said you'd stop talking about debts.
Then call it a promise. One I made with him. But I can tell you one thing.
Tomorrow, whatever happens, don't read that nameplate. Especially not aloud.
As Yeoni looked down, Neo curled his fingers slightly. Instead of saying thank you, he gave their hand a weak squeeze.
All right. I won't read it. But you have to tell me everything in the morning, Neo.
There was no answer. Instead, his breathing grew a little steadier. Supporting his back, Yeoni fell asleep against the pillar.
At dawn, Yundal yawned on the other side of the pillar. He adjusted the glove over his palm and looked toward the others.
Oh.
Moka still snored. Seo Hanbi had fallen asleep sitting up, hugging her umbrella. Yeoni's head drooped against the pillar.
Their shoulder was empty. Only the coat that had covered him remained on the floor. Not even footprints marked the dust.
Everyone wake up. Mr. Cat is gone.
Far away, a door creaked open. Door Six.
